Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-08-21 | AAPL | Underweight | +3.3% | +2.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL, but with a smaller de-risk than the trader proposed: trim ~20–25% of the position near $309–310, taking a standard-weight book to roughly 0.75–0.80x, not the trader's 35–45% cut to 0.55x. Do not add a single share in the $309–311 collision zone (10 EMA 310.35, 50 SMA 310.21, gap lip 310.69, VWMA 308.80). Escalate only on proof: a daily close below $305.59 on >60M shares cuts to ~0.40x, with $289.82 then the rising 200 SMA at ~$281.50 as downstream references, and a ~$294.75 stop (~2x ATR of 7.633) on any residual tactical long. Restore toward 0.90–1.0x only on a volume-confirmed daily close above $314.34 with MACD > −1.194, then scale at $316.8 → $320.3 toward the $329.59 gap fill; horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three seats agree the direction is to reduce and only disagree on size, so the rating is decided by weighing the bear's forward evidence against the cost of trimming this specific franchise at this specific distance from its own re-entry trigger.

What the bear wins, and it is why this is not Hold. (1) The tape is damaged, not merely soft: AAPL closed 309.35 below the 10 EMA (310.35), below the 50 SMA (310.21), below the Bollinger mid (314.34), just under the 310.69 lower lip of the unfilled 7/31 distribution gap (310.69–329.59, ~6% of price overhead), with MACD at −1.574 under its −1.194 signal. The 8/20 push to 320.28 was sold back to 309.35 — a lower high and a failed reclaim. (2) The fundamentals are not an undiscovered catalyst: the 10-Q was accepted 2026-07-31 at 14:01 UTC, and the market then gapped the stock −7.36% to 308.91 on ~132.5M shares (~2.5x normal). Citing revenue +16.1% and 50.06% gross margin as a reason to hold full weight cites what the tape already priced; the market is discounting Q4, not disputing Q3. (3) Earnings quality takes a real haircut: cash taxes paid fell 28.9% while book tax rose 40.7%, so roughly $10.8B of the $35.2B OCF increase is tax timing, and the report itself flags the divergence — that weakens the "FCF +52.5%" proof point the bull leans on. (4) Growth mix is deteriorating beneath the headline: deferred revenue — the annuity layer supporting the multiple — grew only 4.3% against revenue +16.1%, while raw materials inventory rose 260%, which is equally readable as a pre-build or an input-cost hedge and the bull cannot break the tie. (5) The structural bid has thinned: buybacks $62.1B, down 12% y/y, payout 67% of FCF versus 114%, net share count down only 1.1% in nine months — roughly $30B of annual mechanical demand that existed a year ago and no longer does, while $13.3B of newly added intangibles are offset almost exactly by $13.5B of non-current liabilities with no disclosed cash outflow and no footnote. (6) The forward catalyst set runs against holders: two independent sources on 8/20 named the same memory-cost upcycle and Q4 guidance pointing to slower growth and margin pressure, and there is no reported fundamental catalyst until late October.

What the bull wins, and why this is Underweight and not Sell. The franchise is intact and the primary trend has not broken: revenue +16.1% for nine months and +16.4% in Q3, gross margin at a dataset high of 50.06% (+357bp), operating income +21.7%, effective operating margin +152bp YTD, nine-month FCF $110.2B, $146.5B liquidity, net cash nearly doubled to $62.2B with zero new long-term debt and D/E down to 0.78x, and a 200 SMA that has risen every session in the sample to ~281.50 with the 50 SMA 28.7 points above it. The bear's weakest argument is the sequential operating-margin point (H1 34.02% → Q3 32.62%), which is an H1-versus-Q3 seasonal comparison, not a clean year-over-year deterioration; memory-cost inflation is a monitorable forward risk, not yet a reported COGS fact. The buyback cut is genuinely two-sided — discipline and dry powder on one reading, the best-informed buyer standing down at $309 on the other — and insider data is explicitly unavailable in this dataset, so neither side gets to use it.

Where each seat overreaches. The aggressive analyst is right that holding full weight in a zone his own framework calls a coin flip is not neutral, but he pre-loads a re-add at 300–302 where the report concedes the August lows (300.57/302.25) were never repeatedly tested, RSI never reached oversold and no bullish divergence formed — that is falling-knife risk, not asymmetry — and he inflates his evidence with a single-contributor after-close Sell rating and a stale Viking 13F, which are sentiment, not proof; he also conflates magnitude with probability by treating the ~9% to the 200 SMA as the base case when supports sit at 308.80, 307.01 and 305.59 first. The conservative analyst is right that a rising 200 SMA is not a risk control — 7/31 proved that — but tripping a further 20–25% cut on any close below 305.59 "regardless of volume" in a name with ATR 7.633 and a recent 13.3-point single swing (320.28 → 307.01) is whipsaw-prone, and a blanket 45%+ trim without knowing the caller's current weight creates more re-entry risk than it removes. The neutral analyst's triage is the best construction: keep the volume filter, tier the 305.59 trigger, and require a 314.34 reclaim with MACD confirmation before rebuilding — but even 35–40% is too much at this price, for the reason below.

Why I size below every seat's trim range. The objective measure of this trade's expectancy is distance-to-invalidation: the bullish trigger ($314.34 with MACD > −1.194) sits only ~1.6% above spot, against ~9% to the 200 SMA. That is the exact configuration my own record identifies as poor expectancy. The 2026-08-10, 08-11, 08-12 and 08-13 AAPL Underweights each bled alpha in a five-day window (+0.8% to +5.3% of relative underperformance) by trimming momentum decay inside an intact primary trend, and the 08-13 reflection is explicit: do not trim on momentum decay alone without the high-volume distribution print, and 08-12 concluded that an Underweight whose falsification level sits ~3% above entry has poor expectancy — "the honest call was Hold with a sell-into-317 plan, not a 25–50% reduction." Meanwhile the one recent call that paid, the 2026-08-14 Overweight (+2.5% alpha), was built on the franchise legs. The distinction that survives here is that a real distribution print did occur on 7/31 — but it is now three weeks old, the 8/21 pullback volume of 46.9M was below the ~53M average so it was not a fresh distribution day, and the MACD histogram has contracted from −2.29 to −0.38 with price still marginally above VWMA 308.80. That mix justifies reducing exposure toward 0.75–0.80x, not gutting it to 0.55x with a 1.6% re-entry gate.

What would change it. Upgrade toward Overweight on a volume-confirmed daily close above 314.34 with MACD crossing above −1.194 and RSI through 55 — then $316.8 → $320.3, full gap fill $329.59 — and on Q4 evidence that R&D growth decelerates below ~25% while revenue holds >12%, raw materials convert through with gross margin near 50%, and the memory-cost margin narrative concretely reverses in guidance. Downgrade to Sell on a daily close below 305.59 on >60M shares (cut toward 0.40x, with $289.82 and ~$281.50 as references), on a close below 300.57 on above-average volume, on a Q4 gross margin below 48% with a soft guide, or on a close below the rising 200 SMA (~281.50) which would invalidate the primary trend. Stated gaps, not papered over: no valuation multiple, forward consensus or revision trend; no options chain or implied-vol data (so hedge cost must be checked, and the neutral analyst's put-spread/collar preference is unverifiable here); insider transaction data is unavailable and is treated as no evidence in either direction; news coverage is partial; the $13.3B intangible addition against $13.5B of non-current liabilities has no disclosed terms and must be reconciled before any re-upgrade; and the caller's holdings and cash are unknown, so all sizing is a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL weight and every target ($305.59, 289.82, 281.50, 294.75) is technical rather than valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 300.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of +2.9% went against the Underweight, so the directional call was wrong on this window, though five days is far too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis built on a late-October catalyst. It undercuts the headline rating but vindicates the thesis's own core sizing argument — that a re-entry gate only ~1.6% above spot against ~9% to the 200 SMA made a large trim poor expectancy — since price apparently reclaimed rather than broke $305.59. Lesson: when the expectancy math says the falsification level is 1.6% away, that argument applies to the rating itself, not just the trim size; write Hold (or zero trim) rather than an Underweight whose own text calls it poor expectancy.

[2026-08-20 | AAPL | Underweight | +1.1% | -0.1% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL: trim 25–35% of current exposure to a 65–75% core of standard AAPL weight, blended rather than in one print — roughly half near 311.30–313.00 and the balance as limits into 315.52–320.28 if a bounce is offered; complete the trim on a daily close below 310.69. Do not add anywhere between 300 and 320. Reserve only 20–25% of a standard allocation as half-sized, confirmation-based tactical capital: a first tranche only in 302–306 after stabilization above 300.00 (a 299.00 stop can be skipped, two >6% gaps in five weeks), the second only on a daily close above 320.28 on ≥65M shares. A close below 300.00 on expanding volume cuts the residual toward the 289.77 and 281.30 references; a reclaim of 320.28 on real volume, or a Q4 FY26 gross margin ≥50% after the EU take-rate reset, restores the rating. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is settled by convergence, degree is where the money is made, and on degree the three seats overreach in the same direction — they want to sell more than the evidence at 311.30 supports.

What the bear wins, and it is the only dated, undisputed evidence in the debate: AAPL gapped −7.35% on 132.5M shares (~2.5x average) on 2026-07-31 after the 10-Q was accepted, the largest volume print available, and that gap is still unfilled — price sits 6.64% below the pre-report close and 9.66% below the 344.57 high. On 08-19/08-20 AAPL tagged 320.28 and was rejected, closing 311.30, just 0.65 above the session low and 0.61 above the gap's lower edge at 310.69. The advance into it printed 101% and 95% of the twenty-day average volume; a genuine gap-fill breakout prints 130–150%. RSI made lower highs at 72 → 54 → 49 with no bullish divergence, and price is below the 315.52 Bollinger middle/20-day mean, inside the 315.52–320.28 resistance stack. Reward/risk from 311.30 is roughly 0.8:1 to the 320.28 rejection high against the 300.00 base floor. Layered on top: ~35x FY2026 EPS on roughly $8.90, a rising effective tax rate at 17.58% (+219bp), R&D +32.5%, buybacks decelerated 12% to $62.1B, inventory +94% with raw materials +260%, ~$13.3B of intangibles with no matching acquisition outflow and ~$13.5B of unexplained other noncurrent liabilities, and an EU App Store take-rate reset (26% Apple IAP, 20% alternative payments, 15% link-outs, 5% Core Technology Commission) effective October 1 with no quantified revenue impact in the file. An unknown is not neutral when the good news has been bought.

What the bull wins, and why this is not Sell or a 40–50% cut: nothing reported has broken. Nine-month revenue +16.15%, gross margin 49.07% with Q3 at 50.06%, EPS +22.42%, FCF $110.2B, net cash up $28.5B to ~$62.2B with no new long-term issuance, a −63 day cash conversion cycle, and price 10.67% above a rising 200-day at 281.30 with the golden cross intact and the 50-day at 309.85 flat rather than rolling over. And the tape is improving, not deteriorating: the MACD histogram has contracted for six straight sessions from −3.34 to −0.46, the 10-EMA/50-SMA/VWMA are compressed into a 2.16-point band, and VWMA turned up on 08-20 for the first time in ten sessions. The conservative seat's decisive contribution — that with ATR at 7.81 and two >6% single-day gaps in five weeks (06-25, 07-31) a stop is a wish, so size is the binding control — cuts against its own conclusion: it argues for less exposure and smaller tactical size, not for leaning to the top of the cut band while the primary trend is intact.

Where each seat loses. The aggressive analyst is right on the tape and wrong to dress a trim as a high-conviction reload: a 299.00 stop does not define six points of risk in an instrument that jumped 20+ points overnight twice in five weeks, and his limit-only execution into 315.52–320.28 assumes a bounce the market just refused to deliver. The conservative analyst is right on the information vacuum and wrong to near-freeze re-entry until the FY26 filing, which strands the caller holding a full core with no plan and repeats the GOOGL error of ossifying an Underweight into a permanent one. The neutral analyst is the best-balanced and supplies the correct execution note — blended tranches, complete the trim below 310.69 rather than waiting for a bounce — but a 35–45% cut is too large when the falsification level (320.28) is only 2.9% above spot.

That proximity is the deciding arithmetic, and my own record makes it binding. The 06-30, 07-01, 07-13 and 07-20 through 07-24 AAPL Underweights each gave up 3–9% of five-day alpha by trimming momentum decay inside an intact uptrend; the 08-13 reflection codified the fix as requiring the high-volume distribution print, and the 08-12 reflection as sizing the rating by distance-to-invalidation, noting an Underweight whose falsification sits ~3% above entry has poor expectancy. Here the distribution print is real (07-31) but it is twenty sessions old and price has climbed 3.6% off the 300.57 low, price is back marginally above VWMA, and the upgrade gate is 2.9% away against a 3.6% drop to the 300 floor. That is a modestly negative skew, not a decisive one — so trim, but smaller than the Research Manager's 30–50% and smaller than the neutral's 35–45%: cut 25–35%, leaning to the larger end only if 315.52–320.28 is offered.

What would change the rating. Upgrade toward Hold/Overweight on a daily close above 320.28 on ≥65M shares with MACD above zero, or on a Q4 FY2026 print with gross margin holding ≥50% after the EU changes — either restores the trimmed exposure in tranches. Downgrade to Sell on a daily close below 300.00 on expanding volume (cutting to the 289.77 then 281.30 references), on Q4 gross margin below 48%, or if the FY26 10-K shows the $13.3B intangible build is a capitalized commitment carrying amortization or impairment risk, or that inventory days fail to normalize below ~12.

Data gaps, stated rather than papered over: no sentiment report was supplied in this run, no options chain or implied-volatility data (so the hedge the neutral seat favors cannot be priced here), only 20 of 118 eligible news records with zero coverage of 2026-08-13 through 08-17 and no record explaining the 07-31 gap, no consensus forward EPS or valuation multiple, no resolved intangibles footnote, and no portfolio context — so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of the caller's own standard AAPL allocation, and the target is technical, not valuation-derived.

**Price Target**: 305.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY2026 print

REFLECTION:
Alpha of −0.1% versus SPY on a +1.1% raw return says the Underweight call cost essentially nothing in five days, but a five-day window cannot adjudicate a 1–3 month thesis built on a 320.28 invalidation 2.9% away — it is too short to judge, and −0.1% is noise. What the window does support is the sizing logic: neither the 320.28 reclaim nor the 310.69/300.00 breakdown fired, so the "modest negative skew, not a decisive one" framing that produced a 25–35% trim rather than 40–50% was the right posture, while the bear's gap-fill and rejection case remains entirely unconfirmed. Lesson for next time: when the falsification level sits under 3% above spot and the trigger prints are that close, state the entry as conditional on the trigger rather than pre-positioning ahead of it, so the five-day mark reflects a decision instead of a drift.
